leftEvidence.role: Confession, suffering, and the coming Kingdom
leftEvidence.title: Confession and rebuke lead toward the mountain

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Peter calls Jesus the Christ and Son of the living God; Jesus then predicts suffering, death, and resurrection.
points.right: After six days Jesus takes three disciples up a high mountain; his face shines, his clothes become white, and Moses and Elijah appear speaking with him.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Peter rebukes Jesus and is rebuked; disciples are called to take up a cross before a saying about seeing the Son of Man in his Kingdom.
points.right: Peter proposes three tents; a bright cloud overshadows them, the voice names the beloved Son and commands listening, and the frightened disciples finally see Jesus alone.

payload.posture: Matthew places the mountain after Peter’s confession, Jesus’ suffering prediction, discipleship language, and Kingdom sight.

rightEvidence.title: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John

payload.tension: The sequence invites inquiry but does not state that the mountain exhausts the Kingdom promise.
payload.title: Confession, suffering, Kingdom, and the mountain
